decisive_items: multiple cutaneous red papules first noticed at birth
7 × 5 × 6-mm enhancing nodule along posterior temporal dural surface
response.rationale: The constellation of multiple congenital vascular papules, oral anomalies (thickened frenulum, ankyloglossia), and intracranial enhancing nodule with callosal dysgenesis strongly suggests PHACE syndrome, despite GLUT-1 negativity which is atypical but not exclusionary. Other candidates are either too broad (R8, R9), contradicted by normal CBC (R2, R5), or lack the multisystem features (R1, R3, R4, R6, R7).

rejected.why: Nonspecific hemangioma label; lacks syndromic features.
Overly broad congenital disorder; no specific syndrome.
Infantile hemangioma contradicted by GLUT-1 negativity.
Congenital hemangioma typically solitary; does not explain brain and oral anomalies.
Neurocutaneous syndrome too vague; PHACE is more specific.
Vascular malformation does not fit proliferative histology.
Kaposi's sarcoma unlikely in infant; CBC normal.
Tufted angioma usually solitary; lacks brain/oral findings.
